flagship.headline: The Daily Mirror prints Beatlemania
flagship.summary_line_1: The Daily Mirror ran the headline "Beatlemania! It's happening everywhere.. even in sedate Cheltenham" on November 2, 1963, the day after the Beatles' Cheltenham show, per the Beatles Bible.
flagship.summary_line_2: The Beatles Bible says it is believed to be the first use of the word in print, and the clip below is She Loves You.

events.headline: The Band play Up On Cripple Creek on Ed Sullivan
events.summary_line_1: The Band performed Up On Cripple Creek on The Ed Sullivan Show on November 2, 1969, with Levon Helm singing lead, per uDiscover Music.
events.summary_line_2: It was their only Sullivan appearance, and the host introduced them as a new recording sensation, and the clip below is that performance.

events.headline: Stevie Wonder's For Once in My Life enters the Hot 100
events.summary_line_1: Stevie Wonder's For Once in My Life entered the Billboard Hot 100 at No. 79 on the chart dated November 2, 1968, per Billboard.
events.summary_line_2: It went on to peak at No. 2 on both the Hot 100 and the R&B chart, and the clip below is the single.

events.headline: Cream get a platinum disc at Madison Square Garden
events.summary_line_1: Cream received a platinum disc for Wheels of Fire at their Madison Square Garden show on November 2, 1968, during their farewell US tour, per Ritchie Yorke.
events.summary_line_2: The award marked a million sales of the double album, and the clip below is White Room from it.

events.headline: The Beatles finish Hello, Goodbye at Abbey Road
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles added the final overdub to Hello, Goodbye on November 2, 1967, a second bass part from Paul McCartney in Studio Three at Abbey Road, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: The song was then mixed in mono in six attempts, with the last chosen as the master, and the clip below is the finished single.

events.headline: Motown releases the Temptations' (I Know) I'm Losing You
events.summary_line_1: The Temptations' (I Know) I'm Losing You came out on Motown's Gordy label on November 2, 1966, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: Norman Whitfield produced it and it reached No. 1 on the R&B chart and No. 8 on the Hot 100, and the clip below is the single, a Motown classic.

events.headline: The Beatles play two late-added shows in Belfast
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played two shows at King's Hall in Belfast on November 2, 1964, a late booking by promoter Arthur Howes for what had been a rest day, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It was their second and last visit to Northern Ireland, and the clip below is A Hard Day's Night, which was in the 10-song set.

events.headline: The Daily Mirror prints Beatlemania
events.summary_line_1: The Daily Mirror ran the headline "Beatlemania! It's happening everywhere.. even in sedate Cheltenham" on November 2, 1963, the day after the Beatles' Cheltenham show, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: The Beatles Bible says it is believed to be the first use of the word in print, and the clip below is She Loves You.

events.headline: The Beatles play Sheffield City Hall
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played Sheffield City Hall on November 2, 1963, the second date of their autumn tour, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It was their fourth and final City Hall appearance of 1963, and the clip below is From Me to You, which was in the 10-song set.

events.headline: Peter, Paul and Mary top the Billboard 200 with In the Wind
events.summary_line_1: Peter, Paul and Mary's In the Wind was the No. 1 album on the Billboard 200 dated November 2, 1963, per Billboard.
events.summary_line_2: It included Bob Dylan's Blowin' in the Wind, which the trio took to No. 2 on the Hot 100, and the clip below is their version.

events.headline: k.d. lang is born in Edmonton
events.summary_line_1: k.d. lang was born Kathryn Dawn Lang in Edmonton, Alberta, on November 2, 1961, and grew up in Consort, Alberta, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: She became a Grammy-winning pop and country singer-songwriter, and the clip below is Constant Craving.

events.headline: Kai Winding and J.J. Johnson cut tracks for Impulse!
events.summary_line_1: Kai Winding and J. J. Johnson recorded three tracks for The Great Kai & J. J. at Van Gelder Studio in Englewood Cliffs on November 2, 1960, with Bill Evans on piano, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: The album became the first release on Impulse! Records, and the clip below is Blue Monk, one of the jazz tracks cut that day.
